evidence.notes: Formation 'il faut / il pleut'; the impersonal il is the only subject and no plural or other person exists.

patches.value: je/nous + irregular -oir stem + ending (j'aperçois / nous apercevons)

evidence.notes: Formation lists the first-person singular and plural for each -oir verb; the stem alternates between the singular and plural forms, e.g. je dois / nous devons.
Formation is explicit for prendre-type verbs; the double n appears in nous prenons, vous prenez, ils prennent, and the third-person singular has no ending.

patches.value: meilleur / mieux / pire replace plus + adjective or adverb

evidence.notes: Formation 'bon -> meilleur, bien -> mieux, mauvais -> pire'; the irregular form stands in the normal comparative slot, so plus bon and plus bien are excluded.
Examples include vietnamien/vietnamienne, généreux/généreuse, interactif/interactive, faux/fausse; the pattern varies by adjective rather than adding -e.
Formation 'ét- + endings'; être is the only verb whose imparfait stem is not derived from the nous present form.

patches.entity_key: Irregular imperative forms of être, avoir, savoir

evidence.notes: Formation lists the tu/nous/vous imperative forms for the three verbs in that order; they must be memorized rather than derived.
The listed participles (fait, dit, mis, écrit, etc.) fill the participle slot of compound tenses with no regular -é/-i/-u derivation; the context gives a memorization list only.

patches.value: être -> étant, avoir -> ayant, savoir -> sachant

evidence.notes: Formation is stated verbatim for the three verbs; the regular nous - ons + -ant rule does not apply to them.

patches.entity_key: Irregular present subjunctive of aller and vouloir
patches.value: subject + irregular subjunctive stem (aill-/veuill- in je, tu, il, ils; all-/voul- in nous, vous) + ending

evidence.notes: Formation notes an irregular stem in the singular and third-person plural and a different stem for nous/vous; the subjunctive ending follows the subject pronoun.
